records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch-block prisma.workflowReminder.update throws an unhandled P2025 rejection when the reminder row was already deleted by the deleteMany at the top of a concurrent run (retryCount > 1), masking the original error and crashing the request. During overlapping invocations of this endpoint (cron overlap), the second update on a deleted row rejects, the catch block itself throws, and the loop aborts leaving remaining reminders unscheduled for that pass.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The retryCount-based deleteMany branch drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, so the purge matches any WorkflowReminder of any method whose retryCount exceeds 1. The OR branch "{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }" carries no method or scheduledDate constraint, so any workflow reminder (e.g., an SMS one is the only current writer, but the query itself is method-agnostic) with retryCount > 1 is hard-deleted even when its scheduledDate is in the future — and any future writer that sets retryCount on EMAIL/other-method reminders will have those reminders silently deleted by the SMS scheduling cron. Even today, a reminder that fails twice is deleted regardless of date, which is the cap working, but the missing method filter is the sibling condition on the same query that the original code carefully enforced.
records.rationale: In `scheduleSMSReminders.ts`, the `deleteMany` filter was changed to `where: { OR: [ { method: SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: now } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] }`. The second OR branch (`{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`) has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or `scheduledDate`) constraint, so it will delete *any* `WorkflowReminder` row with `retryCount > 1`, regardless of method or scheduledDate. This matches the finding’s concern about method-agnostic hard-deletion and deletion even for future scheduled dates once retryCount exceeds 1.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The retryCount>1 branch of deleteMany drops the method: WorkflowMethods.SMS constraint, so the delete condition matches WorkflowReminder rows of ANY method once retryCount exceeds 1. The predicate is no longer scoped to SMS: any future writer that sets retryCount on an email (or other-method) reminder — or a shared retry helper — causes this SMS cron to permanently delete those rows, silently cancelling email reminders for bookings. Even today it makes the delete semantics dependent on the implicit invariant that only this file writes retryCount, an invariant nothing in the schema enforces.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Rows that failed SMS scheduling twice are hard-deleted (retryCount > 1) with no audit trail, logging, or soft-delete marker. Bookings silently lose their SMS reminders after two transient Twilio errors (rate limit, network blip); neither the operator nor the booker has any record the reminder existed and failed — the `referenceId`/error string in the catch is only console-logged, and the row carrying it is then destroyed. Ops gets no signal that a booking lost a reminder.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] retryCount is incremented via read-modify-write (reminder.retryCount + 1 from the in-memory row fetched at query time) rather than an atomic { increment: 1 } update. If the cron runs concurrently (overlapping scheduler invocations on the same instance or multiple instances), both read retryCount=1 and both write 2, so a reminder that actually failed four times is counted as two and survives two extra retry cycles; the retry cap is enforced only approximately under concurrency.
records.rationale: The diff increments `retryCount` using a read-modify-write pattern (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) in two places (the `else` branch after failing to schedule and inside `catch`). This uses the in-memory `reminder.retryCount` fetched earlier (now explicitly selected) rather than an atomic Prisma update like `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }`. Under concurrent/overlapping executions, two schedulers can both read the same `retryCount` and both write the same incremented value, losing increments and making the `deleteMany` cap (`retryCount: { gt: 1 }`) enforce retries inaccurately.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The deleteMany OR branch matching retryCount > 1 has no method filter, so reminders for any delivery method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP_APP, etc.) that have hit the retry threshold are deleted by the SMS scheduling endpoint, not just SMS ones. When the SMS cron endpoint runs, any non-SMS WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 is hard-deleted; those reminders silently vanish with no send attempt and no audit, and since nothing else in the codebase writes retryCount yet, future failed email retries will be destroyed by an unrelated SMS job. If SMS retries are the intent, the retryCount branch must also constrain method: WorkflowMethods.SMS.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The retryCount increment uses a non-atomic read-then-write (reminder.retryCount + 1) inside a loop over stale in-memory data, and the catch-block update runs against a reminder that may have been deleted earlier in the same run. Concurrent executions of this scheduler (overlapping cron invocations) undercount retries, so failed SMS reminders are retried indefinitely — the retry cap the change exists to enforce is bypassed; the catch-path update on a deleted id throws P2025, aborting the remaining loop iterations so later reminders are never scheduled.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The new `OR: [{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }]` branch in the deleteMany destroys failed reminders instead of just unscheduling them, deleting rows whose scheduledDate is still in the future. Any SMS reminder that failed to schedule twice (retryCount reaches 2) is permanently deleted from WorkflowReminder even though its scheduledDate is in the future — the booking's step loses its reminder record entirely (no cancelled flag, no audit trail), and the attendee silently never gets the SMS; this is unconditional destructive DELETE with no backup/export path, and the loss is silent because the loop below simply finds nothing to schedule.

records.issue_text: [BUG] retryCount is never reset to 0 on successful scheduling, so transient failures accumulate across independent scheduling cycles. A reminder that failed once months ago (retryCount=1), was scheduled successfully on the next run, and then hits a single new Twilio failure is deleted at retryCount=2 — the counter measures lifetime failures, not consecutive retries, so a single transient outage permanently destroys the reminder that the retry-count design intended to allow.
records.rationale: The diff introduces a persistent `retryCount` (DB default 0) that is incremented on failures (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` in both the `else` branch and `catch`), and reminders are deleted when `retryCount > 1` via `deleteMany({ where: { OR: [..., { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] } })`. Nowhere in the diff is `retryCount` reset to 0 on successful scheduling (the success update sets `scheduled: true`, `referenceId`, etc., but not `retryCount`). This makes `retryCount` measure lifetime failures rather than consecutive retries, causing eventual deletion after two total failures even if success

A reminder whose Twilio send failed twice (e.g., transient provider outage) is silently dropped from the database on the next cron invocation; the API still returns `{ ok: true }` and the booking recipient never receives the reminder and no one is told — silent partial success / dropped work.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch block increments retryCount unconditionally, including when the thrown error occurs after a successful send/scheduling update already executed earlier in the try body for the same or prior reminder, double-counting retries against a reminder that was actually scheduled. An exception thrown later in the try body (e.g., by a subsequent await or Prisma update failure) causes retryCount to be incremented on a reminder whose SMS was already dispatched; on the next run, if that reminder's count crosses 1 while it remains unscheduled-eligible, it is deleted by the new deleteMany branch, cancelling a legitimately retryable reminder while the API reports ok.
records.rationale: In the new logic, `retryCount` is incremented in the `catch` block unconditionally (`update` setting `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`). Because the `try` block can already have successfully scheduled/sent the SMS (e.g., `scheduledSMS.sid` exists) before a later awaited operation throws (notably the Prisma `workflowReminder.update` that writes `referenceId`/`scheduledDate` shown in the diff), a failure after the SMS dispatch would still mark the reminder as a retry.
